Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: POC: Trial environment setup — hosted vs dedicated vs VPC (post-call recap)

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great conversation and excited about Acme AI moving forward with a short POC to validate latency and cost for your LLM use case (customer support summarization + retrieval).

Recap / goals we agreed on:
- Success criteria: 99th percentile latency < 500ms for 512-token responses and average per-token cost < $0.0008 for the production prompt mix (see attached POC MAP).
- Evaluation plan: run 1-week controlled trial with 3 representative workloads (low, medium, high concurrency) and a fixed prompt set of 150 examples provided by Priya.
- Environments to evaluate: Redwood Hosted (fastest setup), Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity), VPC trial (network-isolated).
- Ownership: Marissa (redwood) will coordinate setup and infra; Priya (Acme) will provide the prompt set and sample traffic; Alex will own procurement sign-off.
- Timeline: targeted start 2026-10-18, 7 calendar days of steady-state testing, wrap-up review 2026-10-27.

Next steps (action items):
1) Priya: share the prompt set + expected concurrency matrix by EOD 2026-10-12.
2) Acme IT: complete the network checklist if choosing VPC (see network_checklist.xlsx).
3) Marissa: spin up Hosted trial and provision Dedicated sandbox options; send environment access + test credentials by 2026-10-15.
4) Rishi / Neha: prepare recommended config for batching, quantization profile, and KV-cache warm-up script.

Attachments: ACME_POC_MAP.pdf, network_checklist.xlsx (stubs).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite that captures the timeline and owners.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — confirming the high-level success criteria look correct from our side. A couple of clarifications: 
1) For the latency target, is the 99th percentile measured at our egress (i.e., end-to-end from Acme client to Redwood response) or just the Redwood service time? We want end-to-end.
2) Cost target: does that include networking and tokenization overhead, or is that Redwood compute only?

We are leaning toward Hosted first to move quickly, and if latency/regulatory needs require, we’ll evaluate Dedicated or VPC. Priya will push the prompt set today.

Also copied our infra lead (Priya) — she will coordinate the checklist if we try a VPC.

Appreciate the timeline and will aim to hit the 10/18 start.

Subject: Re: POC: Trial environment setup — hosted vs dedicated vs VPC (notes & recommended config)

Marissa / team,

Quick internal note and recommended defaults we should propose back to Acme: 
- Metrics: confirm we will report both Redwood-side service latency and end-to-end latency (we can instrument synthetic client test to capture end-to-end). Mark both in the POC dashboard.
- Cost scope: clarify compute + tokenization + egress for acme-owned network; for Hosted we’ll include compute + tokenization; for VPC they should expect egress/network costs on their side.
- Hosted config: default to 8-concurrency continuous-batching, dynamic KV cache with warm-up script. Quantization: 4-bit where model supports to meet cost target.
- Dedicated sandbox: provision a 2x1 GPU pool (reserve) for steady-state throughput validation; schedule a short warm-up period before measurements.

I’ll draft a one-page config recommendation and drop in the Drive folder.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Product Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
